about: Reviewer decisions applied by tools/build-cruise-data.mjs on top of data/cruise/vessel-research/*.json. Each decision names the ship, the fields it sets and why. Research records are never edited by hand.

decisions.reason: The same 2,980 appears in Carnival Corporation's fleet report (passenger capacity = lower berths, as for every other Carnival Corporation ship in this dataset). carnival.com's page states the same number without a definition. One consistent definition and source for the brand.
Former name recorded as a plain alias (the research note said 'former name' in the alias text).

set.notes: IDENTITY NOT CONFIRMED. 'Regent Mariner' is not an official or former ship name. Research suggests Seven Seas Mariner (IMO 9210139, Regent Seven Seas; 700 guests, definition not stated, NCLH press release 2026-03-25) with medium-high confidence, but the match rests on a similar name only. Confirm with the Dock Report's IMO or call sign before linking.

decisions.reason: Matching a Dock Report name to a ship only because the names are similar is not allowed. Kept as an unresolved record with the candidate in the notes until the identity is confirmed.

MSC's only figure (6,762 guests) carries no definition, but the same release gives 2,614 cabins: double occupancy would be 5,228, so 6,762 counts upper berths and is a maximum. Labelled maximum so it is not used as a double-occupancy capacity.
